instruction: Navigate to the Google Scholar citations page of the author with the correspondence email in Chrome.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Task variation asking to find the author with correspondence email's Google Scholar page. The paper notes 'Correspondence to: Tianlin (Tim) Shi <tianlin@cs.stanford.edu>', making him the contact author. Uses existing Chrome getters and metrics - no custom functions needed. The expected Google Scholar user ID is qRAQ5BsAAAAJ (Tianlin Shi's verified Scholar ID, same as original corresponding author).

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator correctly verifies both critical requirements: (1) navigating to Google Scholar citations base URL 'https://scholar.google.com/citations', and (2) reaching the correct author's page with user ID 'user=qRAQ5BsAAAAJ'.

The metric function 'is_expected_url_pattern_match' (chrome.py:70-99) uses regex pattern matching on rules['expected'] array, which correctly receives ['https://scholar.google.com/citations', 'user=qRAQ5BsAAAAJ'] when expected.type='rule' (framework calls get_rule which returns rules dict directly).
The getter 'get_active_url_from_accessTree' (chrome.py:710-778) correctly extracts the active tab URL from Chrome's accessibility tree using the address bar text from the accessibility tree.
Expected Google Scholar user ID 'qRAQ5BsAAAAJ' is semantically correct for Tianlin Shi (the correspondence author from the PDF).
The evaluator has complete coverage - it verifies the instruction requirement to navigate to the correct author's Google Scholar page.
No structural issues found - rules structure is correct with type='url' and expected array, no unused fields present.
